sections.heading: Metal Roof Repair or Roof Replacement: An Honest Assessment

runs.v: An honest assessment starts with the failure pattern. Repair a metal roof when the damage stays localized at seams, fasteners, or a small section; replace it when panel corrosion exceeds 20 to 25% of the area or seam-connection damage exceeds 25%. Storm damage can lead to leaks that require immediate repair, and emergency repairs for metal roofs may be needed after storm damage or an active leak; wind and hail claims reach roughly 2.8% of insured homes in a year.
What Is the 25% Rule for Roofing?

As a rule of thumb, once damage covers more than about 25% of a roof, replacement usually beats repair. As code, N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 requires a permit to repair or replace more than 25% of the roof in 12 months on buildings other than detached one- and two-family homes.
Is It Necessary to Remove Shingles Before Installing a Metal Roof?

Not always. Metal roofs can be installed over existing roofs if structurally sound, since code allows one recover over a single existing layer, but N.J.A.C. 5:23-6.4 requires removal of a water-soaked or multi-layer roof. A tear-off also exposes the deck, and metal roofs need a proper underlayment to protect the roof deck from moisture.

faqs.q: How long does a metal roof last on a West Orange home?

runs.v: A metal roof lasts 40 to 80 years, with copper at 70-plus years, against 20 years for 3-tab asphalt and 30 for architectural asphalt, per the InterNACHI life-expectancy chart; copper roofing can last over 100 years when installed properly.

faqs.q: Should you repair or replace a metal roof in West Orange?

runs.v: Repair localized seam, fastener, or section damage; replace above 20 to 25% panel corrosion or 25% seam damage, the contractor-consensus thresholds. A Newark Quality Roofing technician identifies the clip system and sealant before sourcing compatible material for a West Orange repair.

faqs.q: Do you need a permit for a metal roof in West Orange, NJ?

runs.v: Re-roofing a detached one- or two-family home is ordinary maintenance under N.J.A.C. 5:23-2.7 and needs no construction permit. Commercial buildings, multi-family, and attached buildings need one once work exceeds 25% of the roof in 12 months, as does structural framing work; confirm with the West Orange construction office before work.

faqs.q: Does a metal roof on a West Orange historic landmark need extra approval?

runs.v: It can. A locally designated landmark or a property in a historic district can need extra review before exterior work, so confirm with the West Orange construction office first. Per the National Park Service, National Register listing alone places no federal restriction on a private owner.

faqs.q: What is the difference between standing-seam and metal-shingle roofing?

runs.v: Standing-seam runs continuous concealed-fastener panels from ridge to eave, while metal shingles are stamped exposed-fastener panels that replicate slate, shake, and tile. Standing seam develops fewer leaks, and both last 40 to 80 years, per InterNACHI.
